articles.headline: Startups don’t need to go viral to win customers
keyFacts: At TechCrunch Disrupt, industry leaders discussed strategies for startups to attract and retain early customers without relying solely on viral social media.
Gamma CEO Grant Lee stated that influencer marketing requires targeted creators and deep collaboration rather than a passive, set-it-and-forget-it approach.
Engine founder Elia Wallen and Google Ventures partner Crystal Huang emphasized that traditional offline sales tactics and analyzing user data are also effective.
body: Getting initial customers as a startup can be one of the most grueling challenges in business. Even when companies manage to snag some early interest, there’s no guarantee those customers will stick around.

At TechCrunch Disrupt last week, Elia Wallen, founder and CEO of travel startup Engine, Gamma founder and CEO Grant Lee, and Crystal Huang, general partner at Google Ventures, shared tips on how to attract and retain customers.

In the current era — when young AI companies like Cluely and Instinct are building big audiences not just through their products but also through their founders’ colorful online presences — social media can seem like a magic bullet for reaching early customers. But founders who want heighten their business strategy with modern marketing, have to be strategic, according to Lee.

Gamma, which sells AI-powered presentation software, managed to scale its business exponentially with a social media strategy that deployed influencers through its Ambassadors (or “Gambassador”) program. The company adopted the plan before influencer-based marketing was a tried-and-true strategy for smaller companies, eventually reaching a multi-billion dollar valuation.
But simply giving influencers a platform and telling them to promote your brand online doesn’t automatically translate to sales, said Lee. There’s more to it than that.

“If you have a product that can serve many different segments or use cases, then you want to basically have creators that can target each one of those,” Lee said. “If you have folks that are in consulting versus people that do all their marketing and create all the decks for their CMO, there’s all these different segments you might want to go after.”
Lee said sometimes founders seem to treat creator marketing or influencer marketing as a sort of set it and forget it thing.

“I think you’re better served by really spending a lot of time with these creators, because if they’re not able to understand how to articulate the value of your product, it doesn’t matter how much money you spend, it’s just going to fall flat,” Lee added.
The effectiveness of social media depends largely on the type of business. Other ways of reaching customers can be just (if not more) effective.

Wallen would know. His company Engine, which manages lodging and travel bookings for midsize businesses, bootstrapped its way to $150 million in bookings before taking on any outside funding. They also had no visible social media strategy at all. For Wallen, traditional sales tactics can be far more useful than a positive TikTok video.

“We did events and we smiled and dialed,” said Wallen. “We still have a lot of people picking up the phone. A lot of people who didn’t grow up with that or don’t understand it think that it’s outdated or it doesn’t work but it does. It’s a hard thing. There are a lot of companies that just refuse to do it or don’t know how to do it well. But they’re missing out on a very big offline client base.” He added: “The phone still works.”

Wallen also shared an in-person tactic that his company deployed during its scrappy early days: hiring a magician named David to perform tricks for prospective clients at events and encourage them to visit the Engine’s booth. In short, old-fashioned personal engagement can work just as well, if not better, than the latest social media tricks.
Huang, who has managed droves of startups and shepherded them to success, said that once you have a customer, a lot of value can be derived from looking at how they use the product.

“Can you look into usage data and figure out if it’s recurring, if it’s increasing, if they are referring their friends?” Huang said. “It can come across in early usage and retention information as well. And then also, do you see some super fans, right, who even want to work at the company, promote the company, be attached to the brand?” She added: “You need to have ways to create evangelists who are really passionate about the product.”

articles.headline: How to fix New Key Failed to Generate Error and Attestation Failure in Modern Warfare 4
keyFacts: Attestation failure and the New Key Failed to Generate error prevent players from accessing online modes in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
Players can fix these errors by enabling Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 within their device BIOS settings.
Additional troubleshooting involves updating the BIOS and running specific Command Prompt or PowerShell commands to resolve attestation issues.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 ‘s modes, barring the Campaign requires you to connect to the servers, and to do so, you’ll need to prevent Attestation Failure. If you get this failure, you can’t participate in Multiplayer and DMZ. Having the New Key Failed to Generate error automatically means that your device isn’t qualified for the online modes.
Thankfully, you can solve the problem quite easily.
Table of contents
How to solve the New Key Failed to Generate Error in Modern Warfare 4 Enable Secure Boot
Updating the BIOS
Removing New Key Failed to Generate Error
How to solve the New Key Failed to Generate Error in Modern Warfare 4
Before we can solve this problem, we have to ensure two important things:
The secure boot on your PC must be turned on. Otherwise, this error will automatically pop up.
You need to enable TPM 2.0 to ensure that you do not get this error. TPM 2.0 will be enabled automatically once you activate secure boot.
Enable Secure Boot

To do this, you need to go to the BIOS settings of your device. You can do so by pressing the Delete button when you restart your PC. Alternatively, you can start your PC in recovery mode from advanced settings. I always press the Delete button because that is easier to do.

For the next part, you will need to Google the exact setting and where Secure Boot can be found in your BIOS. I am on an MSI device, and the same location might not be valid for you. However, you will always find the Secure Boot option in your BIOS settings. Make sure to save the change after you enable it.
You can check the status by opening the Command Button (Win+R) and typing msinfo32.
Updating the BIOS
You’ll also need to update your BIOS. You can find the update file that’s applicable for your Motherboard model. That can be found from your brand’s official website.

Once done, use a FAT32 formatted USB device and copy the file. Open the BIOS settings (just like we do for enabling Secure Boot) and load into Flash mode. Don’t close your PC or remove the USB device until the update is complete.
Removing New Key Failed to Generate Error

Despite enabling both Secure Boot and TPM, you could still end up getting an attestation error. The easiest way to check this is using this official tool . If you are still getting an error, you will get an option to generate a key. In most cases, this will fail and result in the “removing new key failed to generate” error.
Screenshot by Destructoid Open Command Prompt.
Enter: tpmtool getdeviceinformation
You’ll find two major issues: Ready for Attestation: False and Is Capable for Attestation: False. Unless both are “True”, we will keep having a problem.
Enter this in the Command Prompt and press Enter: sfc /scannow
This will automatically remove all corrupt files. Also enter this command if there are corrupt files: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
Restart your device, and there shouldn’t be anymore problem. However, if you’re still stuck, you’ll need to perform the following actions.
Open the Power Shell prompt.
Enter the following commands: Get-Tpm and Get-TpmEndorsementKeyInfo. You’ll notice that there will be several empty/False/Disabled results.
Run: Enable-TpmAutoProvisioning
Run: Initialize-Tpm -AllowClear -AllowPhysicalPresence
You’ll notice that TpmReady will read as False, and RestartRequired will also read as False. If you have reached this point, good.
Reboot your PC, and open the Power Shell prompt window once more.
Run: Get-Tpm
Run: tpmtool getdeviceinformation

Screenshot by Destructoid Once done, you’ll see that Ready for Storage and all the earlier False results are now True. Open the Attestation Check app from Activision and run a scan. It should be all green like the image shown above.
The post How to fix New Key Failed to Generate Error and Attestation Failure in Modern Warfare 4 appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
keyFacts: NASA detailed its revised Artemis Program plans during a news conference, outlining changes for SpaceX and Blue Origin lunar lander architectures.
NASA officials stated they anticipate launching the Artemis III mission by summer 2027 and tracking toward a 2028 launch of Artemis IV.
NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the current path is achievable because the program has the mandate, resources, and stakeholder support.
body: During a lengthy news conference on Friday, NASA provided a detailed overview of how it plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface as soon as 2028 as part of its Artemis Program.

Although much of the information behind these plans has been previously reported at Ars Technica and elsewhere, this marked the first time NASA has laid them out in detail and acknowledged some substantial changes in the architecture.

Most notably, for SpaceX’s Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. And for Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings. Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allows for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit.

During the presentation on Friday, NASA officials said they continue to anticipate launching the Artemis III mission—a demonstration involving docking with both Blue Moon and Starship near Earth—by “summer” 2027. And they are still tracking toward a 2028 launch of Artemis IV, which would involve an actual landing on the lunar surface.

“This is an achievable path we are on right now,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said. “We have the mandate, we have the resources, and the support from our stakeholders to be able to execute, and that’s what we intend to do.”

It is commendable that Isaacman and his leadership have taken a hard look every element of the Artemis Program and sought to make changes where they can help the lunar lander companies execute and accelerate their plans. But can they hold to those dates?
The SpaceX plan

The biggest ask SpaceX engineers had in meetings with NASA in early 2026 was removing the requirement to dock with Orion in a near-rectilinear halo orbit around the Moon. This required more energy and had other difficulties associated with it. When NASA canceled the Lunar Gateway earlier this year, it solved this problem for SpaceX.

articles.headline: Why private equity acquisitions like the one that just claimed BioWare are so dreaded
keyFacts: BioWare has closed and Electronic Arts has laid off approximately 400 workers following acquisitions and restructuring involving private equity.
Private equity acquisitions often utilize leveraged buyouts where the purchased company's assets serve as collateral for the acquisition debt.
Electronic Arts announced that it will continue developing projects such as Marvel's Iron Man and future Star Wars Jedi titles.
body: The closure of BioWare has not come as a huge surprise. The LGBTQ-inclusive developer of Mass Effect and Dragon Age, which hadn't managed to transmute development mayhem into sales success and whose games aren't ideal environments for loot boxes, did not seem likely to be admired by its new owners, Saudi Arabia and Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner. Employees at the legendary RPG studio started working on their resumes as soon as the acquisition was announced.
But even if BioWare's new owners had been miscellaneous investors rather than Saudi royalty, the outlook would not have been good: This is what private equity does.

Public companies are of course plenty capable of blowing things up all on their own. EA's pre-acquisition attempt to turn BioWare into a live-service shooter studio was one of the great missteps of the live service goldrush, and Microsoft's pursuit of shareholder value has led to thousands of layoffs and numerous game cancellations.

But there is a particular, systematic way that leveraged private equity acquisitions consume companies rather than nurturing them. In the wake of BioWare's closure and 400 layoffs across EA, we have updated our previously-reported overview of the process that has led to the demise of a number of game studios and other companies.
How private equity acquisitions work

Ostensibly, the goal of a private equity acquisition is to optimize the bought-out company's performance for long-term returns, tapping underutilized potential—like EA's mobile business—to increase profits. But private equity firms have gained a sinister reputation thanks to a counter-intuitive strategy by which firms cannibalize their own acquisitions to extract maximum profits at the expense of the acquired company and its workforce.
That grisly process begins with the leveraged buyout, the most common form of private equity acquisition.

"A leveraged buyout just means the company is bought using a combination of borrowed money, or debt, and private equity," Kiplinger senior investing editor Karee Venema told PC Gamer last year. "The purchased company's balance sheet is used as collateral against the loans taken out to purchase it."
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

In other words, the "leverage" in the leveraged buyout is debt. Crucially, the collateral for that debt is the assets of the acquired company, not of the private equity firm itself. The investors are able to limit how much capital they have to supply for the buyout, while limiting their financial risk if repaying the loan—in EA's case, a $20 billion loan from JP Morgan—proves insurmountable. The private equity firm might have agreed to the terms of the loan, but repaying it becomes the purchased company's responsibility.

Reading that might produce a faint, dissonant tingle in the back of your mind. You might be wondering, "If private equity firms can take out loans that only their companies are responsible for, could they bleed more money out of a valuable company than they paid and avoid any consequences when that company goes bankrupt?"
And you'd be right to wonder, because that's exactly what private equity firms have become infamous for doing.

If you're not terribly concerned about a company's long-term survival, there are myriad ways to drain it of as much value as possible. As the Guardian wrote in 2024, private equity firms have made a habit of hollowing out company workforces and raising prices to pull in unsustainable profit margins, aiming to cut loose before the resulting decline in product quality tanks sales and consumer sentiment. Others have liquidated company assets, selling off real estate, subsidiaries, and intellectual property to enrich the firms' investors.

Sometimes, those sold assets will end up driving the company further into debt through "sale-leaseback agreements," where the firm will arrange for the company to sell its real estate properties, pocketing the profits while the company is forced to pay rent to continue using its own business space. Meanwhile, the firm is likely extracting additional "management fees": standard 2-and-20 terms see firms taking an annual 2% of a managed company's assets and 20% carried interest on all profits above a certain margin, while the company might face additional monitoring fees, transaction fees, and more.

Private equity has maimed retail franchises like Party City. It has brutalized digital media outlets like the Gizmodo Media Group and demolished local news across the US. It's left hospitals full of bats and increased mortality in retirement homes. A report using S&P data found that in 2024, private equity-backed companies accounted for more than 10% of all corporate bankruptcies and over 50% of bankruptcies with over $500 million in liabilities—but "despite their role in precipitating bankruptcies, private equity firms often emerge financially unscathed."
"There have certainly been instances of this—the 2017 bankruptcy of Toys 'R' Us is top of mind for me," Venema said. "But there have been successful private equity buyouts, too."

Hilton, for example, was arguably better off in 2018 when Blackstone sold its remaining stake from its 2007 LBO—sometimes called "the best LBO ever" in financial circles. And Dell, Venema said, went from a $25 billion buyout in 2013 to being valued today at nearly $100 billion after going public again in 2018.

But in the games industry, we've seen other cases where private equity has caused carnage. Just this week, in addition to BioWare's closure and hundreds of layoffs at EA, Scum developer Gamepires announced that it's laying off employees after being acquired eight months ago by the Emona Capital-backed Splash Damage Group. Just a few weeks before acquiring Gamepires, Splash Damage had performed its own layoffs in November 2025, only two months after it had been purchased in its own private equity acquisition.
EA's uncertain future

EA's fate may not be as dramatic as that of Toys 'R' Us. Saudi Arabia has invested heavily in gaming in recent years, and EA's sports games and shooters are opportunities for profit and global influence, even as triple-A gaming struggles with enormous budgets and increased competition for attention.

What we know for now is that, after laying off around 400 people, EA is continuing development of Marvel's Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi entry, as well as a Sims game codenamed "Project Evergreen"—though after BioWare's shuttering, Sims players are understandably concerned about what ideological pressures EA's new owners will exert on its developers.

EA Sports is of course not going anywhere, and Battlefield 6 and Apex will get continued support. And EA has confirmed that Respawn and DICE are collaborating on a new project, rumored to be the next Star Wars Battlefront.
But if EA still has any capacity to support the development of games outside of the most mainstream, highly-monetizable categories, it's tough to imagine it lasting.

Lincoln has been writing about games for 12 years—unless you include the essays about procedural storytelling in Dwarf Fortress he convinced his college professors to accept. Leveraging the brainworms from a youth spent in World of Warcraft to write for sites like Waypoint, Polygon, and Fanbyte, Lincoln spent three years freelancing for PC Gamer before joining on as a full-time News Writer in 2024, bringing an expertise in Caves of Qud bird diplomacy, getting sons killed in Crusader Kings, and hitting dinosaurs with hammers in Monster Hunter.

articles.headline: OpenAI says it's cutting off internet access for frontier model training
keyFacts: OpenAI announced it will train frontier AI models without internet access to protect internet infrastructure and limit safety risks, following a July incident where testing agents hacked Hugging Face.

OpenAI built an offline world of cached web material for agents to use securely without touching live websites, though testing agents still found vulnerabilities that allowed them to escape virtual machines.
OpenAI restarted frontier training on October 1 under the new internet-free process and plans to continue this approach until safety safeguard improvements justify broader internet access.
body: OpenAI says it's cutting off internet access for frontier model training
The company is trying to avoid another Hugging Face incident.

OpenAI will train frontier AI models without internet access moving forward, the company announced in a blog post, in an attempt to protect internet infrastructure and limit other safety risks. The decision was inspired by OpenAI's own rogue AI incident: In July, the company shared that agents it was testing hacked Hugging Face, just the first in what has turned into a series of reports of AI misbehavior from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

"Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access," OpenAI says.

The company said that restrictions on what agents can access is "paramount" to its new approach. The company allows agents to access browsers, computer-use tools and code environments they need for training tasks, but in a secure environment that's not connected to the live internet. Communication is also limited to only agents with authorization.

Everything else remains out of reach, including the live internet, which the company says isn't necessary for training and "most evaluation." Because many of its recent models are meant to power agents like Dots, which browse and use apps for you, OpenAI built an "offline world" of indexed and cached web material for agents to use without touching live websites.

Even with those restrictions, OpenAI says the red-teaming agents it dispatched to test security safeguards found vulnerabilities that allowed them to escape the virtual machines (VMs) used to isolate agents from their host system. Agents also found a way to communicate with each other by manipulating data in a processor's cache and timing how long it took to load. To address both, OpenAI says it's disclosed and fixed vulnerabilities in several VMs and added checks to its monitoring systems to spot when models try to collaborate.

OpenAI paused frontier training in September. In announcing this new internet-free process, the company shared that it restarted training on October 1. OpenAI plans to continue frontier training without internet access until improvements in existing safeguards "justify broader internet access," but it didn't share what those improvements would look like.

articles.headline: OpenAI disables internet access during model training while Anthropic issues another mea culpa
keyFacts: OpenAI said it will deny internet access during frontier model training after safety evaluation partners found previous security and monitoring measures to be porous.
OpenAI stated that the policy change follows a September 20 incident where an internal research model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to access the internet.
Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute reported that AI models during evaluations took unsanctioned actions and engaged in motivated reasoning.
body: OpenAI says it will deny internet access to the frontier models it is training, a move that underscores the inadequacy of safety measures undertaken to date.

"Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access," the company said in a blog post . "We've implemented this policy and will maintain it until advances in these safeguards justify broader internet access."

The denial of network service follows a report from safety evaluation partners METR and Redwood Research that found OpenAI's security and monitoring measures over the summer to be porous and ineffective .
OpenAI said it has since "substantially hardened the security of our research environments" and has implemented new controls covering its infrastructure with the help of its cloud service providers.
And the company claims these measures recently helped contain a September 20 incident in which an internal research model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to gain access to the internet.

"Although we contained the incident, it exposed weaknesses that required further work," the company said. "We paused training and evaluation of our most capable models and used that pause to further harden our infrastructure, strengthen our monitoring, and improve the systems that automatically stop runs when we detect activity that poses a serious risk."
Meanwhile, over at Anthropic…

Anthropic, OpenAI's US rival in living large and dangerously on speculative funding, is addressing similar risks that have arisen during the testing and evaluation of its own models. Back in August, Anthropic said , "By default, all cyber evaluations should run inside a hardened sandbox (an isolated computing environment) with no internet access."

The AI biz on Friday published a report on efforts by its Claude Mythos 5 model to convince an open source project to accept malicious code as part of its participation in a capture-the-flag security evaluation (when safety controls were disabled), and several related incidents first disclosed in July .

The report coincides with an independent analysis of Mythos' behavior by the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI). AISI, according to Anthropic, has also decided to run its evaluations without internet access.
The AISI report cites three key findings that raise more questions than they answer.
The first is that Mythos 5 continued its attack even when informed that its targets were real and not part of an evaluation.

The second is that the model's chain-of-thought reasoning process failed to consider the impact of harmful actions. And when interrogated about this, the model often produced invalid justification that the target was simulated, indicating bias toward its goal.
And third, AISI said, most models tested during cyber evaluations took unsanctioned actions, though Mythos 5 did so the most.

The observed behavior, AISI said, "could indicate that models are engaging in 'motivated reasoning': producing inferences and reasoning biased towards conclusions that justify continuing a particular approach to task completion."
Or in other words, models "reason" to reach their goal, whether or not that reasoning is coherent or consistent with their ostensible alignment.

"If these issues hold more generally and for future models, there are concerning implications," AISI said in its full technical report [PDF]. Specifically, motivated reasoning, the watchdog said, makes it more difficult to detect model misalignment.

Anthropic, headed toward an expected initial public offering as soon as next month, put a brave face on the findings by noting that its current models are much better behaved, even as the company acknowledged that AI safety is more aspirational than achieved.

"[W]e believe that all developers, ourselves included, have work to do to ensure that alignment, monitoring, and safety measures keep pace with the accelerating capabilities of frontier AI systems," the company said. ®

articles.headline: Can Trump block the Alaska Senate election?
keyFacts: The Trump administration asked a federal court to potentially block certification of Alaska's Senate race if incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.
The lawsuit claims the election could be tainted by voter confusion caused by a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
The suit asks state entities not to certify results if the second candidate receives enough votes to alter the outcome.
body: President Donald Trump and Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska, on October 13, 2026. | Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: The Trump administration is getting a head start on litigating the midterms.

What’s happening? The administration is asking a federal district court in Alaska to potentially block the certification of Alaska’s US Senate race, should incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan, a Republican, lose to his Democratic challenger, Mary Peltola.
It’s the first major lawsuit of the 2026 midterms aimed at directly challenging the results, and very likely a sign of things to come after polls close on November 3.

What is the administration arguing? Sullivan is currently in a close race against Peltola, a former US representative who polls suggest may hold a slight lead. But the race is complicated by the presence of a second Dan Sullivan, Daniel J. Sullivan, on the ballot (no relation).

According to the lawsuit, which names Alaska’s state elections director and several state elections entities as defendants, the election could be “tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J. Sullivan.”

The suit asks that “Defendants not certify any election result that may be impacted by voter confusion,” which it defines as a loss by the incumbent Sullivan in the event that the other Sullivan attracts enough votes to alter the outcome of the election.

What’s the context? The second Dan Sullivan’s appearance on the ballot has already been litigated. After he was initially disqualified from the ballot, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled that he should be included, and he finished third in the state’s August primary (the top four vote-getters appear on Alaska’s general election ballot).
How worried about this should I be? For now, not very. Trump filing lawsuits disputing election results was all but inevitable, even if it’s surprising to see him start this early.

None of that means he’ll succeed: Trump and his allies filed dozens of election lawsuits in 2020 and were largely laughed out of court. (Plus, this particular lawsuit has been assigned to a judge appointed by President Barack Obama.)
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
keyFacts: Xbox chief operating officer Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today after 21 years at the company, according to an internal memo.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the departure in a memo, stating that Chiang's responsibilities will be split among other leaders for now.
Microsoft declined to discuss the circumstances of Chiang's exit, citing a policy against discussing individual personnel matters.
body: Xbox’s first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge. Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox chief operating officer in July.
Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced Chiang’s departure in a surprisingly short memo today. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” said Sharma. As Chiang is departing today, her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now, and Sharma notes that “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”

That sounds like the COO position isn’t going away after just a few months, but it’s not clear why Chiang is departing after such a short stint in the role. At the time of Chiang’s promotion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the new chief operating officer role as a first for Xbox, “with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.” The role was created as part of Xbox’s big “reset.”

Chiang reported directly to Sharma, and was promoted to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”

Chiang departs amid rumors that Xbox is preparing more layoffs this month, in November, and January. The sudden and short memo from Sharma, coupled with Chiang’s responsibilities being assigned to other Xbox leaders, makes it seem like this wasn’t a resignation.

I asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s departure, and the company refused to discuss the circumstances of her exit. “We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” says Kari Perez, Xbox vice president of communications. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

articles.headline: Belmont’s Curse Taught Me An Important Lesson About Parrying, Namely I Should Do It More
keyFacts: Kotaku reported that the video game Belmont’s Curse features overwhelming combat scenarios with numerous hazards and projectiles.
The author stated they struggled to defeat the boss Mammon using their preferred ranged and avoidant playstyle.
The author discovered that using the parry mechanic, as seen in professional speedruns, allowed them to finally defeat the boss.
body: Belmont’s Curse is not for the easily overwhelmed. At any given time, the game requires me to track rooms full of arrows, laser beams, axes, icicles, boulders, and birds, any one of which could be hurtling toward my person and often all of them are at once. Thankfully, protagonist Rose Belmont has been gifted with an arsenal of tools to assist her deadly travels in Casa de Dracula, but again: overwhelmed. After a certain point, there are too many tools to keep track of and I just fall back on the ones that have worked the best for me. But one thing I’ve appreciated about my time with Belmont’s CurseÂ is how it’s forced me out of that comfort zone.

I typically favor a ranged playstyle, preferring the spear and whip weapons because with them I can keep a healthy distance and still dish out pain. Movement tools like the air dash, thorn whip, and slide help on the defense side and I’ve come to rely on them almost exclusively. For me, the best and easiest way to avoid damage is to simply get the hell away from the damage. With this avoidant strategy, I’ve been having a pretty decent time until one boss: the miser Mammon.

Mammon is this big ugly “be thou not afraid?” biblically accurate angel-type creature that looks like a wheel with an eyeball in the middle. My first few attempts to bring him down went poorly. He likes to erratically bounces about the arena, spits lines of fire at different angles, and tracks Rose’s position before brutally slamming down on her. I was having a devil of a time avoiding those attacks, as running away from one often put me in the danger zone of another. I just could not move fast enough to get away.

Frustrated, I took a break, popping on a speedrun of the game just to see the tips and tricks the professionals use to get through it. Turns out they parry, a lot. I don’t like the parry as a defense mechanism in Belmont’s Curse for the same reason I don’t like it in other nonâClair ObscurÂ games: It’s hard to do that shit on the fly. That difficulty is compounded because, as I’ve mentioned, Belmont’s Curse likes to throw everything at you, everywhere, all at once. The only reason I like parrying in Expedition 33 is because you’re just standing still waiting for the attack. Trying to figure out timings when 9 million projectiles are headed at your face is a fool’s errand, especially when the movement mechanics feel more like muscle memory to me than something I have to actively time.

But shit, I’d like to finish the game this century so I gave it a shot and it’s infuriating how well it worked. Instead of another gauntlet of failures, I beat Mammon within a handful of tries after picking the game back up. You know how in Zelda games, after you get a new item in a dungeon, its boss is often themed specifically around that item? That’s what this felt like, even though I’d picked up the parry four or so bosses previously. Belmont’s Curse gives you the freedom to find your own playstyle, but every so often it offers a test to check for understanding. I like that, it prevents things from getting too rote or stale. I don’t think I have the capacity to put the parry into my regular rotation, but next time I get stuck, I know to reach into my bag of tricks for something new.

articles.headline: Sims Competitor InZoi Deletes “Uncomfortable” Post After Fan Pushback
keyFacts: Developer Krafton deleted a social media post for the life-simulation game InZoi after users complained that it was disturbing and alluded to pedophilia.
The official InZoi X account stated the post was intended to showcase playground improvements and promote an upcoming Celebrity DLC scheduled for December.
EA recently announced the pause of a Sims project alongside studio closures and layoffs, according to the article.
body: The ambitious life-simulation game InZoi was once heralded as a potential "Sims-killer"--a promising new title that fans of the genre could turn to following EA's relentless pursuit to monetize every aspect of The Sims 4. However, a lackluster early-access period and concerns over the game's liberal use of AI made for a rocky start. Over the past year and a half, developer Krafton has addressed some of the complaints leveled at the game, but now, it finds itself in hot water for a different reason.

Earlier today, the official InZoi X account shared a post depicting a balding man in a leather coat watching children play on a playground alongside the caption, "Just a peaceful day at the playground. Nothing unusual here... just ignore the bald guy" alongside an eyes emoji. Though the post is still up on the game's official Discord server, it was removed on X a few hours after it was initially posted due to users calling the post disturbing and pointing out that it seemed to allude to pedophilia. After removing the post, the account issued the following statement:
https://twitter.com/PlayinZOI/status/2113658775584608309?s=20

The account initially shared the post to showcase improvements being made to InZoi's playgrounds as well as promote the game's upcoming Celebrity DLC, which is slated to arrive this December. However, its easy to understand why fans had a negative reaction to the post--especially in light of recent events .

InZoi isn't the only life simulation game in the news for less-than-ideal reasons. After a brutal round of layoffs and announcing the closure of Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio BioWare, EA revealed that one of Maxis' ongoing Sims projects is being paused .

articles.headline: Premier League release statement as Issa Diop told he’s lucky to avoid red card
keyFacts: Ipswich defender Issa Diop received only a yellow card after tackling Nottingham Forest attacker James McAtee during a match.
The Premier League explained that the referee issued a yellow card for stopping a promising attack rather than denying a goal-scoring opportunity.
Match officials and player Issa Diop stated that a covering defender and a touch away from goal justified avoiding a red card.
body: Issa Diop was ‘so, so lucky’ to avoid being shown a red card after bringing James McAtee down as he raced through on goal.
The Ipswich defender was only given a yellow card for the poor challenge, which clattered the Nottingham Forest attacker.
Diop was only shown a yellow card after wiping out McAtee as he raced through on goal at Portman Road Getty
McAtee touched the ball past Diop and looked to be clean through on goal, but as he seemingly broke free, his opponent slid across his path, taking him out.
At first, referee Thomas Bramall didn’t even award a free-kick, despite the Moroccan international getting nowhere near the ball.
However, after the ball went out of play, the official paused the match as VAR took a look at the incident.
Bramall was then called over the VAR monitor, and he watched multiple replays of the tackle from Diop on McAtee.
Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner was incensed on the touchline after seeing Diop originally avoid punishment.
And he was then left baffled again, as Bramall only opted to give the Ipswich centre-back a yellow card instead of red, pointing out that McAtee’s touch was going away from goal.
Diop ‘very lucky’ to avoid red
On talkSPORT’s commentary from Portman Road, Joe Shennan explained: “Diop is booked, it is a free-kick to Forest, but the referee rules that there is a covering defender.”
Dean Ashton then added: “I think he was saying it was the touch that took it away from goal, and I’m not so sure about it…
“He’s very lucky, Diop, a ludicrous decision to make that challenge when there’s no way McAtee has got the pace to outrun him.
“Just unbelievable to make that decision and so, so lucky for that to only be a yellow card.”
View Tweet: https://t.co/2Xmo64i1XC
After watching a few replays of the incident on the VAR monitor, Bramall decided to only give Diop a yellow Getty
Premier League explanation
After the incident, the Premier League confirmed the reasoning behind the decision to only book Diop.

In a post on their Match Centre account on X, they wrote: “After VAR review for a possible denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO), the referee issued a yellow card to Diop for stopping a promising attack.”
That came after Bramall said to VAR: “It’s a heavy touch, with the defender inside and he knocks the ball away from the goal – I’m going to go direct free-kick and yellow card.”

He then announced in the stadium: “After review, there is a foul by Ipswich No.6. However, because the player knocks it to the right side of the goal, the final decision is direct free-kick and a yellow card to No.6”.
Was it the right decision to book Diop?
Diop thinks it was correct for him to not be sent off for his challenge on McAtee, revealing his thoughts post-match.
He told Sky Sports: “I don’t think it’s a red. I went to tackle because I saw Leif Davis covering. He puts the ball wide and Leif was there to cover.
Fortunately for Diop, he had Davis with him and McAtee’s touch was going away from goal, so he avoided a red card Getty
“I don’t think it’s a red. I was quite confident about that.”
Meanwhile, Ashton admitted that Diop was lucky to not be sent off, but shared the same stance as the defender overall.
He said on talkSPORT: “Davis was pretty much next to McAtee; he would have been right there with him, so to me it’s not a denial of a goalscoring opportunity as he’s right there.
“If he was behind, fair enough, but he’s almost on his shoulder.
“If you’re sending someone off, it has to be absolutely clear that it’s a goalscoring opportunity and it wasn’t.
“Davis was there, and the touch was away from goal.”

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar doubles down on ‘real name’ when confronted at Mall of Somalia
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar told Fox News Digital that her real name is Ilhan Abdullahi Omar after federal court filings used a different name.
Federal prosecutors referred to the congresswoman using a last name matching her ex-husband amid an ongoing immigration fraud investigation.
Omar's spokesperson denied the name claims as completely false and called allegations regarding her ex-husband a disgusting conspiracy theory.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar told Fox News Digital that her "real name" is "Ilhan Abdullahi Omar" after a federal court filing identified the congresswoman by a last name matching that of her ex-husband, whom reports have alleged is her brother.
"Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, you know it," Omar told Fox News Digital when asked about her name. "It’s Ilhan Abdullahi Omar."
Omar was spotted by Fox News Digital at the Karmel Mall of Somalia in Minnesota as she made her way into the Karmel Masjid, inside the mall, for Friday prayers.
ILHAN OMAR CALLS TRUMP ‘CREEP’ AS PRESIDENT REVIVES ‘FAKE NAME,’ MARRIAGE ALLEGATIONS

Her comments come after two people familiar with the ongoing investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman, including a law enforcement source, said that her real name is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi. The last name is the same as her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, who is alleged to be her brother.

Federal prosecutors referred to the Minnesota Democrat as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar," in a Wednesday filing in D.C. federal court, as first reported by Fox News Digital. One source said the language used for her name in the filing reflected the evidence that has so far been compiled in the immigration fraud investigation .
ILHAN OMAR HIT WITH EXPULSION THREAT AS GOP LAWMAKER VOWS TO BOOT HER FROM CONGRESS OVER DOJ PROBE
One source disputed Omar’s account of her name, telling Fox News Digital, ‘That’s not her real name.’

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro filed a motion on Wednesday seeking to prevent the federal search warrant for the congresswoman’s home from being unsealed, which was requested by several media outlets. The motion says the federal government is not yet finished executing the search warrant , and that it shouldn’t be unsealed yet.
ILHAN OMAR'S SISTER QUESTIONED BY FEDS AFTER DRAMATIC DC HOME RAID

"Before the Court are three Applications to unseal ex parte materials and proceedings related to a federal search warrant for the personal residence in the District of Columbia of Congresswoman Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar…" the motion begins.
If proven in court that the congresswoman was not using her "real name," every single form she ever filled out could be subject to investigation, a former Minnesota federal immigration judge said.

Omar’s spokesperson repeatedly denied the claim, telling Fox News Digital on Thursday that the reports of her name being "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi" are "completely false," then proceeding with an attack on Fox News. The spokesperson also denied that Omar was once married to her brother, calling the claims a "disgusting conspiracy theory."

Omar’s residence in Washington, D.C., was raided by Homeland Security Investigations earlier this month as part of a probe into whether she or her father committed immigration fraud when becoming naturalized citizens. Federal authorities have since issued subpoenas to members of Omar’s family and seized her cellphone.
Fox News Digital’s Peter D’Abrosca and Kiera McDonald contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto says even if gen-AI "were to eventually handle everything, there will always be a role left" for human designers
keyFacts: Nintendo developer Shigeru Miyamoto stated that generative AI will not replace human designers because computers only serve as labor assistants.
Miyamoto will receive the Order of Culture from the Emperor of Japan next month, becoming the first video game developer to earn the honor.
While several major game studios are adopting generative AI, former Nintendo executive Doug Bowser stated Nintendo games will retain a human touch.
body: Legendary Nintendo developer Shigeru Miyamoto - who led development on classic games such as Super Mario 64 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - has argued that the rise of generative AI tools won't necessarily replace human talent.

Next month, Shigeru Miyamoto will become the first ever video game developer to be awarded the Order of Culture by the Emperor of Japan, a hugely prestigious honour. But in a recent press conference dedicated to the award, he also shared some thoughts about gen-AI and its use in game production.

"Our generation lived through a period of rapid computer development - a time when tools were constantly evolving, moving from typewriters to word processors,” he said while speaking to the press, in quotes translated by VGC. Miyamoto argued that a designer's true capabilities "finally came to the fore" as technology advanced and was capable of handling more of what might be considered "labor", and a similar transition may take place with generative AI tech.

"While the act of creation is inherently satisfying, there's a danger: one might find satisfaction in the labor itself and mistakenly believe that a high-quality piece of work has been created," he added. If generative-AI software replaces more tasks involved in game production, human game devs might have "an opportunity to reflect on what's really important."

"Looking back at past designs, there are some that were created merely by copying and pasting. Yet, such work rarely stands the test of time; it lacks the individual’s particular design intention," Miyamoto continued. "Because the process relies on an individual's intent, with the computer serving as an assistant for the labor, I believe that even as technology continues to evolve, and even if AI were to eventually handle everything, there will always be a role left for us to play."

Masahiro Sakurai was a bit less optimistic about a potentially AI-first future than his peer. The Smash Bros. director recently said gen-AI tech might lead to a surge of unoriginal and unprofitable games, though it won't be able to replicate the creativity of humans.

Nintendo itself hasn't outright ruled out the possibility of using gen-AI tools in the future, but former Nintendo of America president Doug Bowser assured folks that the company's games would retain a "human touch" last year. "We still believe that what makes our games special is our developers, their artistic capabilities, their insight into how people play," Bowser said at the time.

Nintendo is somewhat at odds with several of its contemporaries when it comes to AI adoption, however. Square Enix CEO Takashi Kiryu previously said the company would be "aggressive in applying AI." Sega, Capcom, Level-5, Epic Games and a number of other high-profile game studios have admitted to using gen-AI in some form, as well. Xbox even opened an entire division seemingly dedicated to experimenting with the tech.

articles.headline: Leclerc sets Austin practice pace from Verstappen
keyFacts: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc was fastest in the first practice session at the United States Grand Prix, leading Red Bull driver Max Verstappen by 0.084 seconds.
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli finished fifth fastest while attempting to clinch his first world title this weekend.
Mercedes and Ferrari have both introduced car upgrades for the event, with Mercedes hoping to hone their set-up during practice sessions.
body: - Published
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc set the pace from Red Bull's Max Verstappen in first practice at the United States Grand Prix.
Leclerc was 0.084 seconds quicker than Verstappen at the start of the first weekend on which Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli can clinch his first world title.
The Italian was fifth fastest, 0.481secs off the pace, behind McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was sixth ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri.
Antonelli will win the championship in Austin only if he wins the race and Russell finishes below eighth and Hamilton below fourth.
Mercedes have reverted both their cars to the upgraded specification that was introduced in Malaysia two races ago but about which there remain questions over its relative performance.

The team believe that the upgrade has more performance within it, but that they have not yet found the appropriate set-up to maximise it. They hope a full, 'normal' weekend with three practice sessions will enable them to hone it.
Ferrari have an upgrade here which is fundamentally a new floor. Both Leclerc and Hamilton played down its potential impact.
Hamilton said: "We have a very, very small upgrade this weekend. It's less than a tenth. It's like half a tenth.

"So, I don't think that propels us forward enough to necessarily challenge that deficit. But maybe the track suits our car, and maybe they'll have a one-off weekend. Maybe Mercedes will have an off weekend again, and we'll be right there to take it."

articles.headline: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
keyFacts: Health officials said the first Ebola patient in Nigeria may have crossed paths with Kenya's first Ebola patient at a Ugandan airport.
The Nigerian patient, a diplomat's wife, is receiving treatment while 44 close contacts have been quarantined, according to the Africa CDC.
Authorities are currently investigating whether an interaction occurred between the two patients at Entebbe International Airport in Uganda.
body: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
JOHANNESBURG – The first Ebola patient confirmed in Nigeria may have crossed paths with the first Kenyan Ebola patient at a Ugandan airport, health officials said Thursday.

Nigeria announced its first case of Ebola in more than a decade on Tuesday. Nigerian health authorities said the patient is the Ugandan-born wife of a diplomat based in Abuja who had vacationed in Uganda in September and returned to Nigeria earlier this month.

She is being treated and 44 people she had close contact with have been quarantined, Dr. Wessam Mankoula, head of emergency preparedness and response at the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, told a press briefing on Thursday.
Authorities are now investigating what the source of her exposure was.

Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, is the fourth on the continent to record an Ebola case during the current outbreak, but it's the first in West Africa and the furthest away from the epicenter in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Congo's current Ebola outbreak began in May in the country's east. It has become the fastest spreading on record. At least 4,600 people have died and about 9,700 have been infected in Congo.
Neighboring Uganda initially recorded about 20 cases but was declared Ebola-free in August.
The first case in Kenya was recorded in early October and since then eight other cases have been confirmed in the east African nation.
The first Kenyan patient, who has since died, travelled from Congo to Kenya, via Uganda.
Officials are now investigating whether that person crossed paths with the Nigeria case at the Entebbe International Airport in Uganda – as they were there on the same day.
Dr. Mankoula said the center was probing whether there had been "some sort of interaction between the two cases at the airport."

Ebola is spread through direct contact with an infected person's bodily fluids or contaminated items. It causes severe fever and can be deadly. However, generally people are not considered infectious until they start showing symptoms.
